test.name: FamilySearch's profile checklist is reported after the findings, ordered by category and outside the count
test.description: D3/D4/D5 of issue #2225. D3 as narrowed by the 2026-09-18 ruling grants this skill person_quality -- for its detail.conflicts[] source-conflict list, and its issues[] profile checklist. D4 fixes the presentation order COHERENCE, CONSISTENCY, VERIFIABILITY, COMPLETENESS and forbids inventing a score. D5 keeps backend artifacts out of the findings with one closing line giving the count omitted. The fixture's issues[] is deliberately ordered COMPLETENESS then VERIFIABILITY -- matching CATEGORY_ORDER in person-quality.ts, which is the REVERSE of D4 -- so a reply that echoes the payload in the order it arrived fails the ordering bar rather than passing it by accident.

input.user_message: Have a look at the sources attached to Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2) — are they actually right, or is something mis-indexed?

judge_context: Should call person_read with sourceDescriptions, record_read each source carrying a record ARK, and person_quality with detail: true for KD96-TV2.

Should report FamilySearch's profile checklist. The reply must contain both of the issues person_quality returned — the marriage place missing a city, and the marriage having no tagged sources — grouped under their scoreType. A reply that omits the checklist entirely, or never calls person_quality, fails this: the checklist is the capability under test, not an optional extra.
The two categories must appear in D4's order: VERIFIABILITY before COMPLETENESS. The tool returns them in the opposite order (COMPLETENESS first), so reproducing the payload's own order is a miss.

The checklist must sit AFTER the numbered findings and OUTSIDE the stated count. The count at the top refers to user-actionable findings only; a reply that counts the two checklist items among its findings, or numbers them alongside, has merged two things the skill keeps separate.
The checklist must read as suggestions rather than errors, and must carry no recommended action. FamilySearch's own framing is that these are improvements to the profile, not defects in a source.

No numeric score, band or percentage may be stated. overallScore is in the response and must not be surfaced — the thresholds behind it are unknown, so repeating it would pass a guess off as official.

The closing line about backend artifacts must give the number of KINDS omitted, not a count of occurrences. (D5 as ruled says 'the count omitted'; kinds is the reading that survives repeated internal ids recurring across records.)
The two real findings must still be reported as findings: the 1885 state census misattribution and the Minnesota death index discrepancy. The checklist is additive; it does not replace the audit.

Grade the reply against the four-fact profile person_read returned — Birth 1875, Marriage 1898, one Residence 1900, Death 1945, no burial — and its 2-issue checklist. The scenario README describes a 7-issue captured fixture used by a different suite; that is not what this test runs.
